LUCIEN MALLET’S PHONE

On 28 May 2030 at 08.14, at Belleville métro station, customs broker Rémi Vidal (49) fell from the platform edge onto the tracks and went under the incoming train.

The passenger who made the emergency call and was first to the platform edge was Lucien Mallet; in his statement he said, “The man was looking at his phone, the crowd pushed, he fell.” The morning papers called him ‘the hero of the platform’.

The platform camera’s view of that spot is blocked by a pillar.

There’s partnership insurance, yes; if he dies, the share comes to me. I knew you’d ask that. But nobody liked Rémi; in 2019 he had an accident, a girl died, he was acquitted. Her family shouted ‘murderer’ at him in court.

An old ruling pulled from the branch archive:

· 3 March 2019, Bagnolet. The car driven by Rémi Vidal hit 16-year-old Camille Mallet on a pedestrian crossing; Camille died.
· The breath test result was lost; Vidal was acquitted.
· At the verdict hearing the girl’s father, Lucien Mallet, was removed from the courtroom.
2019 ACCIDENT FILE

The call log started before the push; the cab camera showed the hand, the autopsy the bruise on the back, the card log the long wait, and the old accident file the connection. The phone, opened on two grounds, gave the five-week list of times.
The first to run is not always the first to see; sometimes it is the one who knew in advance. Put the seconds in order.
Belleville — May 2030

For five weeks Lucien Mallet noted the morning times of Rémi Vidal, who in 2019 killed his daughter Camille on a pedestrian crossing and was acquitted, and measured the platform’s blind spot. On 28 May he waited on the platform from 07.36; he put the phone to his ear and started the emergency call, and seven seconds later pushed Vidal in front of the train with his free hand, then shouted for help.
Who is responsible for Rémi Vidal’s death?
